newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian steel firm bankruptcy held off again.
newsitem.headline: Belgian steel firm bankruptcy held off again.

text.p: A Belgian commercial court on Tuesday ruled against declaring whether or not Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq SA was bankrupt after hearing a report by two experts on the company's viability, the Belga news agency said.
Belga said the report showed that Clabecq was still viable in its current form until mid-1997 in view of its order book.
Its activities should be reduced and a restructuring considered thereafter, it said.

After a one and a half hour meeting the court appointed a company receiver who should draw up a financial plan based on the full resumption of work from January 6 and start-up of the furnace from January 4.
Clabecq filed for bankruptcy last Thursday after its majority shareholder, Belgium's southern Walloon region, withdrew its support.

The fate of the loss-making company, which employs nearly 1,800 people, appeared to have been sealed last Wednesday when the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc ($46.8 million) rescue plan by the Walloon region for Clabecq.
The Commission said the subsidies went against EU rules which only allow steel sector aid for environmental reasons, for research and development or for company closure.
